# `Q-12-18` — Invalid Glob Pattern in Listing `contents:`

> A listing `contents:` pattern is not a valid glob and matches
> nothing.

## What this means

Every `contents:` entry is parsed as a glob pattern. This warning
fires when the parse fails; the message carries the parser's
reason. The malformed entry contributes no items, and the rest of
the listing still resolves.

## Why this happens

Two causes account for nearly every occurrence:

- **`**` that is not a whole path segment.** `**` means "zero or
  more directory levels" and must stand alone between slashes:
  `posts/**/*.qmd` is valid, `posts/a**b.qmd` is not.
- **An unclosed character class.** `[0-9]` is a class;
  `posts/[0-9.qmd` is a parse error.

## How to fix

Rewrite the pattern using the supported vocabulary:

| Syntax | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `*` | any characters within one path segment |
| `?` | one character, never `/` |
| `**` | zero or more whole path segments |
| `[abc]`, `[a-z]` | character class |
| `[!abc]` | negated character class |
| `[*]` | a literal `*` |
